hook: Some bacterial tRNAs read the codon CGG as tryptophan, not arginine, as computation had predicted
summary: Computational predictions suggested some bacteria decode the arginine codon CGG as tryptophan. In an E. coli cell-free system, candidate tRNAs from distant bacteria restored fluorescence and enzyme activity, and mass spectrometry showed tryptophan in place of arginine. Proteomics of Anaerococcus prevotii agreed. Direct evidence covers one native species and a test-tube system, not living cells of other predicted bacteria.
title: Sense-to-sense changes in bacterial genetic codes: Experimental validation by cell-free translation and native-host proteomics
